previous_review: REJECT (rev 1): 'Illegal ZExt' crash for mask lanes wider than 32 bits (CGBuiltin.cpp:23254) and getZExtValue assertion on a negative 128-bit constant lane (:23216). Both are fixed by 6cd475ae65b8.

6cd475ae65b8 logic. Constant path: APInt::urem(NumSrcElts) is exact for any width. Run-time path: the index is reduced with urem in the mask lane's own type, then CreateZExtOrTrunc to i32. The urem is skipped only when NumSrcElts >= 2^LaneBits, i.e. every value the lane can hold is already < NumSrcElts, so skipping is exact (for example 8-bit lanes with 2N = 256). For LaneBits >= 64 it always reduces, and NumSrcElts fits in the type. Correct.

Reproducers: logs/20-F019-review/q2.c (v2l/v2d with a long long mask, riscv32) compiles through -emit-llvm and through the back end. q.c (riscv64 __int128 constant mask {-1,2}) gives shufflevector <1,0>. A new q3.c (riscv64 __int128 run-time mask) compiles and reduces the low word with & 3.

Wide-lane values: logs/20-F019-review/w.c, wc.c. Shapes: v2l one and two vectors with run-time masks, including 2^32+1, 2^32+3 and -(2^32-1); v2d with a v2l mask; v2d with a v2ul mask; v4l; v4i; 128 x i8 signed and unsigned, one and two vectors; constant masks c1-c5 with 2^32+1, -(2^32-1), -1, INT64_MAX, 0x8000000000000003, INT_MAX, -8, and 128 x i8 {-1,127,-128,5,-3}. Reference: a host scalar model (-DREF); host x86-64 GCC's own __builtin_shuffle gives the same hashes. GAP9 GCC accepts every case and matches the reference on GVSoC at -O0 and -O2. clang 20-F019-rev2 matches the reference in every group on: generic rv32imc_zfinx -O2; Xpulpv2 -O0/-O2 on the patched GVSoC, except k2/k2u (see the next item). Generic -O0 does not fit the testbench RAM and was not run. On the stock GVSoC, c5 also differs; its code uses pv.shuffle2.b (B113 simulator bug), and it passes on the patched GVSoC.

k2/k2u (128 x i8, two vectors, run-time mask, the 2N = 256 no-urem case) are wrong only with Xpulpv, at -O0 and -O2. The cause is pre-existing B112, not this change. clang's IR is correct: 'extractelement <128 x i8> %m' then 'zext i8 to i32' as the index. The back end selects the sign-extending pv.extract.b for that zext (128 pv.extract.b feeding address adds, no andi 255), so mask bytes >= 0x80 become negative offsets. k1, the one-vector case, passes only because urem 128 becomes andi 127, which hides the wrong extension. Generic builds pass k2. The minimal proof is logs/20-F019-review/zext-extract.ll: 'zext(extractelement <4 x i8>)' and '<2 x i16>' give pv.extract.b/.h on both int-20 and rev2. F029's B112 fix should add k2 (wc.c) to its checks.

Worker's mixt.c: same root cause as B112 (distinct symptom, same selection bug). With int-20 at -O2 +xpulpv2, the byte-wise read of the 16-byte vector becomes word loads plus pv.extract.b a4,a1,k (sign-extending), feeding 'H = (H ^ c[i]) * p' where c is unsigned char, so bytes >= 0x80 are sign-extended. Nothing involves __builtin_shuffle or compares. The common defect: any zext of a v4i8/v2i16 extract_vector_elt is selected as sign-extending pv.extract.b/.h (zext-extract.ll). B112's 'lane compare' wording is one symptom of it. Recommend widening B112/F029 to 'zext(extract_vector_elt) selected as pv.extract.{b,h}' and adding mixt.c, zext-extract.ll and wc.c k2 to F029's checks.
